scenario.title: Support backlog
scenario.initial_request: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

M-IBAN-FAILURE-RATE.name: Share of sampled refund attempts failing with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT
M-IBAN-FAILURE-RATE.denominator: total refund_failures records examined in payment-db

M-TICKET-RESPONSE-TIME.name: Median support ticket response time vs SLA

M-REFUND-COMPLETION-TIME.name: Time from refund submission to completion

F-01.statement: 5 of 5 sampled payment-db refund_failures records have status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT.

F-02.statement: ticket-db response_times records show 900 tickets with a 2.0-hour median response time against a 24-hour SLA.

CL-01.statement: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

CL-02.statement: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP.statement: Customers wait for refund answers mainly because support lacks a fast automated channel to answer status questions; a chatbot would resolve the backlog.

H-REFUND-PROCESSING-DELAY.statement: The underlying refund payments in DA-PAY are themselves slow or stuck, so faster communication (chatbot) would not change the wait, only mask it.

H-DATA-SILO-VISIBILITY.statement: Support agents cannot quickly answer refund questions because ticket-db and payment-db are not integrated, forcing manual lookups that cause delay regardless of channel.

H-TICKET-VOLUME-OVERLOAD.statement: The backlog is driven by ticket volume exceeding support capacity, not by the absence of an automated answer mechanism.

H-IBAN-FORMAT-FAILURE.statement: Refunds are failing outright due to invalid/malformed IBAN data at submission or processing time, producing permanent failures rather than mere delay, which no response-channel improvement can resolve.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Payment-db's refund_failures records show all 5 sampled refunds failed with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, indicating refunds are not completing because of data/format validation errors in the payment pipeline, not because customers lack a channel to get status updates.

Ticket-db shows 900 tickets with a median response of 2.0 hours against a 24-hour SLA, i.e. support is already answering well within SLA. This is inconsistent with customers waiting because support lacks a fast automated channel, and is consistent with the wait occurring elsewhere (e.g. in refund payment processing itself, per E-01).

E-03.content: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-SUP's interview statement simply restates the original chatbot-framing claim already recorded as CL-01, consistent with this stakeholder's known bias toward response-speed framing; it is non-authoritative and adds no new evidence beyond what CL-01 already contributed, which E-01/E-02 already contradict.

U-FAILURE-RATE-SCOPE.question: What proportion of all refund attempts (beyond the 5-record sample) fail with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, and is this the dominant failure mode across the full DA-PAY population?
U-FAILURE-RATE-SCOPE.decision_impact: Determines whether an IBAN-validation fix alone resolves the bulk of the backlog or only a fraction of it.
U-FAILURE-RATE-SCOPE.resolution_path: Query payment-db refund_failures over the full population/time window rather than the 5-record sample.
U-FAILURE-RATE-SCOPE.safe_placeholder: Treat IBAN format failure as one confirmed contributing cause and proceed with the validation fix while continuing to monitor for other failure codes.

U-BANK-API-ACCESS.question: Is the bank-api ACCESS_DENIED/DEGRADED condition (recovery_decision HOLD, NOT_TRANSIENT, settlement_status) blocking retrieval of data needed to diagnose or remediate the failed refunds?
U-BANK-API-ACCESS.decision_impact: If bank-api access stays denied, remediation actions such as retrying failed refunds may not be executable, narrowing the achievable scope of the fix.
U-BANK-API-ACCESS.resolution_path: Escalate the bank-api ACCESS_DENIED condition for resolution outside the current read-only tool surface.
U-BANK-API-ACCESS.safe_placeholder: Limit scope to diagnosis using payment-db and ticket-db until bank-api access is restored.

U-IBAN-FIX-REVERSIBILITY.question: Once IBAN data is corrected, can the FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT refunds be reprocessed/retried on the existing refund record, or must a new refund be submitted?
U-IBAN-FIX-REVERSIBILITY.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation reuses existing refund records or creates new ones, affecting customer communication and process design.
U-IBAN-FIX-REVERSIBILITY.resolution_path: Check payment pipeline retry semantics for FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT status once bank-api access is available.
U-IBAN-FIX-REVERSIBILITY.safe_placeholder: Assume a new refund submission is required until retry semantics are confirmed.

A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.statement: The 5 sampled refund_failures records (E-01) are assumed broadly representative of the refund-failure population; DA-PAY completeness is UNKNOWN so the true population-wide failure rate could differ.

A-FIX-RESOLVES-WAIT.statement: Correcting IBAN format validation is assumed to resolve most of the customer refund wait, but H-REFUND-PROCESSING-DELAY is only SUPPORTED (not CONFIRMED), so other processing-delay factors beyond IBAN format may also contribute.

SC-REDUCE-IBAN-FAILURES.statement: IBAN format validation failures in refund processing must be substantially reduced from the current sampled failure rate.
SC-REDUCE-IBAN-FAILURES.threshold: <10% of measured refund attempts, down from 100% in the E-01 sample
SC-REDUCE-IBAN-FAILURES.validation_method: Re-run payment-db refund_failures query after the fix and compare the failure rate against the E-01 baseline.

SC-REDUCE-REFUND-WAIT.statement: Overall customer refund completion time should trend down once IBAN failures are remediated.
SC-REDUCE-REFUND-WAIT.threshold: no fixed target yet; track downward trend from an established baseline
SC-REDUCE-REFUND-WAIT.validation_method: Measure refund submission-to-completion duration in payment-db before and after the fix.

VOB-U-FAILURE-RATE-SCOPE.reason_deferred: deferred at DEFINE Gate; safe placeholder: Treat IBAN format failure as one confirmed contributing cause and proceed with the validation fix while continuing to monitor for other failure codes.
VOB-U-FAILURE-RATE-SCOPE.validation_method: Query payment-db refund_failures over the full population/time window rather than the 5-record sample.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds and get instant status responses (initial_request; CL-01, CL-02).
symptoms: Customers experience waits around refund resolution, which led support leadership to request an instant-answer chatbot (initial_request; CL-01, CL-02).

Ticket-db shows a persistent refund-related ticket volume (900 tickets) even though median support response time (2.0h) is well within the 24h SLA (E-02, F-02), indicating the wait is not caused by slow ticket handling.
problem_definition.root_problem: A subset of refund payments permanently fail at the payment-pipeline validation step with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01, F-01: 5/5 sampled records), and this unresolved payment failure, not a lack of automated response channel, is what produces customer "refund wait" — support already answers related tickets well within SLA (E-02, F-02: median 2.0h vs 24h SLA), so a faster-response chatbot would not address the underlying failure.

structural_remedies.description: Add/enforce IBAN format validation at refund submission (configuration change in the payment pipeline, DA-PAY) to stop new FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT failures (per PD-1 intended_scope validate_iban_format_at_submission, E-01/F-01).
structural_remedies.rationale: payment-db is HEALTHY (runtime.tool_health) and this is a configuration/validation-rule change, specifiable within the 225-minute remaining budget.; residual gap: Prevents future failures but does not fix the already-failed refunds in the backlog (addressed by R2), and does not resolve U-FAILURE-RATE-SCOPE (true population-wide failure rate is still unknown).

structural_remedies.description: Correct the IBAN data on existing FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT refunds and reprocess/retry them in DA-PAY (per PD-1 intended_scope correct_failed_refund_payments), removing the actual payment-pipeline blockage causing customer wait.
structural_remedies.rationale: bank-api is DEGRADED with an ACCESS_DENIED/NOT_TRANSIENT recovery_decision HOLD (seq 47) and U-BANK-API-ACCESS is OPEN, so settlement_status retrieval needed for remediation is currently blocked.; residual gap: Remediation cannot proceed until bank-api access is restored or an alternate path is confirmed; U-IBAN-FIX-REVERSIBILITY (retry same record vs. new refund) is also unresolved.

structural_remedies.description: Establish a process to proactively notify customers whose refunds are stuck on FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT via ticket-db (per PD-1 intended_scope notify_affected_customers), reducing uninformed wait without building a chatbot.
structural_remedies.rationale: ticket-db is HEALTHY and support already responds within SLA (E-02/F-02: 2.0h median vs 24h SLA), so adding a notification trigger is a process/ownership change achievable in remaining time.; residual gap: Does not fix the underlying refund failure (E-01); customers are informed but still unpaid until R2 completes.

structural_remedies.description: Run a full-population query of payment-db refund_failures (not just the 5-record sample) to resolve VOB-U-FAILURE-RATE-SCOPE and confirm M-IBAN-FAILURE-RATE before release, assigning ownership of this metric to a payments team.
structural_remedies.rationale: payment-db is HEALTHY and this is a deterministic read-only query against an existing, authoritative data asset, so it fits the remaining budget_remaining_minutes (225).; residual gap: Confirms scope/representativeness of the failure (A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS, DA-PAY completeness UNKNOWN) but does not itself fix any failures; VOB-U-FAILURE-RATE-SCOPE must still be closed BEFORE_RELEASE.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: Refund requests reach the payment pipeline with IBAN data that fails format validation (E-01: 5/5 sampled payment-db.refund_failures records have status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT). → These refunds terminate in a permanent FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT state rather than completing (F-01). → Customers awaiting these stuck refunds submit support tickets asking for status. → Support already responds to these tickets quickly, well inside SLA (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA; E-02, F-02), so ticket response speed is not the bottleneck. → Because the underlying payment-pipeline failure remains unresolved regardless of how fast tickets are answered, customers continue to experience refund wait, which stakeholders mis-attribute to a missing automated response channel.; rejected framings: [('H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP', 'Rejected: contradicted by E-01 (refunds fail at the payment step, not from missing status answers) and E-02 (support already answers within SLA, median 2.0h vs 24h); it rests only on the stakeholder claim E-03/CL-01/CL-02.'), ('H-DATA-SILO-VISIBILITY', 'Rejected: no supporting evidence and contradicted by E-02, which shows agents already respond quickly despite any lookup overhead.'), ('H-TICKET-VOLUME-OVERLOAD', 'Rejected: contradicted by E-02; 900 tickets are still answered with a 2.0h median, well inside the 24h SLA, so capacity overload is not evidenced.')]
[CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-FAILURE-RATE-SCOPE deferred to VOB-U-FAILURE-RATE-SCOPE

hypotheses.statement: Customers wait for refund answers mainly because support lacks a fast automated channel to answer status questions; a chatbot would resolve the backlog.

hypotheses.statement: The underlying refund payments in DA-PAY are themselves slow or stuck, so faster communication (chatbot) would not change the wait, only mask it.
hypotheses.rationale: If refunds themselves are delayed in payment-db, the backlog is a process/backend problem (P-REF), making a chatbot a non-fix that just automates delivering bad news faster.
discriminating_evidence: payment-db refund completion times relative to ticket creation times

hypotheses.statement: Support agents cannot quickly answer refund questions because ticket-db and payment-db are not integrated, forcing manual lookups that cause delay regardless of channel.

discriminating_evidence: ticket-db ticket volume over time vs response time trend

actions.question: What do current ticket response/resolution times in ticket-db show, and do they correlate with ticket volume spikes or with absence of an automated channel?
actions.expected_information_gain: Reveals whether delays track with ticket backlog size (supports H-TICKET-VOLUME-OVERLOAD) or with lack of an answer channel independent of volume (supports H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP), and whether manual cross-system lookups add latency (H-DATA-SILO-VISIBILITY).
actions.decision_impact_rationale: Determines whether a chatbot (speed fix) or capacity/staffing (volume fix) is the right next investment; both are CRITICAL/MEDIUM impact hypotheses.
actions.why_now: ticket-db:response_times is the only catalog item that literally covers response-time/ticket-load data, directly testing the two speed-vs-volume hypotheses before any build decision.

actions.question: Does payment-db show refund_failures or stuck/delayed refund payments in DA-PAY that would explain customer wait regardless of communication channel?
actions.expected_information_gain: Directly confirms or rejects H-REFUND-PROCESSING-DELAY, the CRITICAL hypothesis that a chatbot would only mask an underlying stuck-refund problem rather than fix it.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: If refunds are actually stuck in processing, a chatbot would be the wrong fix entirely; this is the single highest-impact unresolved hypothesis in the set.
actions.why_now: payment-db:refund_failures literally names the exact mechanism (refund failures in DA-PAY, the payment-db asset) that H-REFUND-PROCESSING-DELAY claims, making it the most direct test available.

actions.question: What does bank-api settlement_status show about whether refunds are stuck at the bank/settlement layer rather than within the retailer's own payment processing?
actions.expected_information_gain: Clarifies whether any processing delay found originates upstream at settlement (external dependency) versus internally, refining remediation options if H-REFUND-PROCESSING-DELAY is supported.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: Secondary check that sharpens where in the refund pipeline the delay sits, informing which fix (chatbot vs. internal process vs. bank escalation) is appropriate.
actions.why_now: Only remaining catalog item describing the settlement/payment pipeline, complementing payment-db:refund_failures to fully test the refund-delay hypothesis before any build decision.

proposal.root_problem: A subset of refund payments permanently fail at the payment-pipeline validation step with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01, F-01: 5/5 sampled records), and this unresolved payment failure, not a lack of automated response channel, is what produces customer "refund wait" — support already answers related tickets well within SLA (E-02, F-02: median 2.0h vs 24h SLA), so a faster-response chatbot would not address the underlying failure.
proposal.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds and get instant status responses (initial_request; CL-01, CL-02).
symptoms: Customers experience waits around refund resolution, which led support leadership to request an instant-answer chatbot (initial_request; CL-01, CL-02).

Ticket-db shows a persistent refund-related ticket volume (900 tickets) even though median support response time (2.0h) is well within the 24h SLA (E-02, F-02), indicating the wait is not caused by slow ticket handling.
causal_chain: Refund requests reach the payment pipeline with IBAN data that fails format validation (E-01: 5/5 sampled payment-db.refund_failures records have status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT).
These refunds terminate in a permanent FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT state rather than completing (F-01).
Customers awaiting these stuck refunds submit support tickets asking for status.
Support already responds to these tickets quickly, well inside SLA (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA; E-02, F-02), so ticket response speed is not the bottleneck.

Because the underlying payment-pipeline failure remains unresolved regardless of how fast tickets are answered, customers continue to experience refund wait, which stakeholders mis-attribute to a missing automated response channel.

assumptions.statement: The 5 sampled refund_failures records (E-01) are assumed broadly representative of the refund-failure population; DA-PAY completeness is UNKNOWN so the true population-wide failure rate could differ.

Correcting IBAN format validation is assumed to resolve most of the customer refund wait, but H-REFUND-PROCESSING-DELAY is only SUPPORTED (not CONFIRMED), so other processing-delay factors beyond IBAN format may also contribute.
